newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania hopes to snare $1 billion in investment.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania hopes to snare $1 billion in investment.

text.p: Tanzania will hold its first international investment forum in November and organisers hope that contracts worth at least $1 billion will be clinched.
A list of 102 investment projects worth $950.85 million will be promoted at the forum, said Harish Pant, chief technical advisor of the U.N. Development Organisation (UNIDO).
They include projects in agro-industry, tourism, mining, infrastructure, chemicals, paper, textiles and pharmaceuticals.

A team of Tanzanian experts have identified an additional 70 technology requests from local entrepreneurs worth $154 million which will be promoted in the November 5-8 forum in the capital, Dar es Salaam, Pant said.

"At present, Tanzania heavily depends on its imports, and trade balance is totally sided in favour of the imports. There is a tendency of the local investor to promote trading rather than manufacturing because it is less risky and the returns are faster," Pant told reporters late on Monday.
Projects holding the most attraction for foreign investors are in the agro-industry and tourism sectors, Pant said.

He added that agro-industry requests for medium- to large-scale investment were led by the demand for coffee processing and handling systems, cotton seed oil and edible oil refining technology, and technology for dairy products and fruit processing and canning.

Chemical and pharmaceutical sectors needed help to launch production plants for a wide variety of goods, including medical textiles, technology for disposable syringes, machines for pharmaceutical production and industrial adhesives, he said.
Tanzania's mining industry required mining equipment and investment in gemstone cutting and polishing, Pant said.

A list of 13 target countries have been approached to send investment teams to the forum and the response so far has been encouraging, Pant said, naming the countries as Britain, the United States, Germany, South Africa, Spain, India, Mauritius, Canada, Sweden, Denmark, Malaysia, Lebanon and South Korea.
"We are targetting 150 foreign companies who we'll bring face to face with 300 local investors," he said.

Since the introduction of trade liberalisation in 1985, the Tanzanian government has initiated economic reforms that have included cutting controls on foreign currency trading, allowing market-driven interest rates and creating the independent tax administrator Tanzania Revenue Authority.
The U.N. is providing $750,000 in organisational and logistical support for the Tanzania forum.
